cited_checks.note: The attested Clopper--Pearson binomial-tail inversion gives conservative (at-least nominal) two-sided coverage, matching the stated Bin(N,p), p in [0,1], total-noncoverage claim.

Hoeffding Theorem 1, specialized to independent Bernoulli summands, gives the stated upper tail; applying it to complemented summands gives the lower tail. The vacuous beyond-support range extends the displayed inequality to all t>0.
